title: Spline surge curation log — admission smoothing experiment
content:
Topline: quick scratchpad of the spline-based surge curation idea + first synthetic runs. This is a working log — experiments are noisy, many open questions. Notes to self and collaborators below.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- We see recurring microbursts that break our batching heuristics and cause p99 spikes (~2-3x baseline).
- Straight admission control with fixed token/time caps reduces spikes but hurts tail throughput.
- Idea: apply a light-weight cubic-spline smoothing on the ingress rate window to modulate admission thresholds adaptively ("spline-curation"). Intuition: smooth transients without over-reacting to short-lived noise, allow short high-QPS spikes to pass if local trend suggests falloff.

Experiment setup (synthetic):
- Hardware: 4x A100-80GB (dev cluster), single model instance per GPU.
- Model: open-13B, quantized int8 path, KV-cache warm in steady-state runs.
- Sequence length: avg 64 tokens, max 512 clamped.
- Baseline admission policy: sliding-window EWMA (alpha=0.3) based threshold, max_concurrency=8, batch_timeout=12ms.
- Spline policy: maintain last N=9 samples (100ms sampling), fit cubic spline (fast online incremental interpolation) and compute predicted window QPS. Admission threshold is weighted average: 0.6*spline_pred + 0.4*ewma.
- Arrival patterns: three traces generated — (A) Poisson (control), (B) single microburst (1s 6x baseline), (C) clustered bursts (random bursts every 20–40s, duration 500–1200ms).
- Run duration: 30m per trace, repeated 5 times for variance estimate.

Metrics captured:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), mean throughput (req/s), queue length distribution, batch size histogram, dropped/queued counts, CPU for admission controller, additional scheduling lag introduced.

First-run results (averaged):
- Trace A (Poisson): baseline vs spline — negligible difference. p99: baseline 180ms, spline 178ms; throughput identical within 0.5%.
- Trace B (single microburst): baseline p99=760ms, spline p99=420ms (≈45% improvement). Mean throughput: baseline 98% of peak; spline 96% (slight drop). Batch size histogram shows spline preserves larger batches during tail of burst vs baseline which collapsed into many small batches.
- Trace C (clustered bursts): baseline p99=620ms, spline p99=380ms. However, observed 3s-long tail events (rare) where spline over-predicts and admits too aggressively causing a small cascade on an overloaded GPU; happened 2/25 runs.

Observations / interesting artifacts:
- Spline smoothing reduces oscillatory corrections common with EWMA-only admission. When a burst spikes and quickly drops, EWMA lags and then aggressively clamps; spline predicted trend often shows downward slope earlier -> softer clamp.
- CPU overhead of spline calc ~2.2% of one CPU core at 1000 samples/s — acceptable in host admission process. Consider moving to vectorized SSE/AVX path for extra headroom.
- Rare mispredictions (over-admit) occur when burst is followed by a second larger burst within sampling window — spline sees upward curvature and temporarily raises threshold. Could mitigate by adding conservative clipping (max delta per-window).
- Batch timeout behavior: with spline we can lower batch_timeout by 2–3ms without p99 regression in most traces; this gives slightly better median latency.

Quick graphs (ASCII histograms / notes):
- Batch size (baseline vs spline) for Trace B: baseline modal=3, spline modal=5; baseline right-shift to many 1/2-size batches during the burst.
- Queue length spike: baseline peaked at 28 reqs, spline peaked 16.

Open questions / next experiments:
1) Stability under multi-tenant noise: current runs single-tenant; need to run on heterogeneous workload mixes (short-LLM p50~60ms + long-generation p50~600ms).
2) Parameter sweep: N (sample window) from 5–21, weight mix spline:ewma from 0.2–0.8, and clipping thresholds. Want simple heuristic that generalizes.
3) Secondary safety: add a conservative floor based on instantaneous max token arrivals to avoid over-admit when an incoming super-burst escalates. Test with compound bursts (back-to-back bursts of increasing magnitude).
4) Long-term drift: how does spline behave when diurnal slowly rising baseline occurs? EWMA will adapt; spline might under-react if window too small. Need to simulate ramp traces.
5) Telemetry: add a "spline-confidence" metric (residual between spline and last sample) emitted to Console for rollouts.

Patch notes / implementation TODOs:
- PoC is in PR linked above (serving-runtime/pull/689) — internal-only, not production. Add unit tests for corner cases (back-to-back bursts).
- Create Linear ticket to add clipping heuristic + telemetry (RED-2987).
- Add a small e2e canary: enable on 1% of Dedicated nodes (pinned pool) for 48h, monitor p99 and dropped queue ratios.

Quick conclusions (working):
- Spline-based smoothing is promising for microburst shaping: big wins on p99 while keeping throughput close to baseline.
- Risk is over-admit on certain burst patterns; mitigations look straightforward (clipping + fallback to EWMA on low confidence).
- Next: parameter sweep + multi-tenant tests, then limited canary.

Notes to self: log raw sample buffers from runs that triggered cascade (save to /tmp/spline_debug_*) and attach to PR. Coordinate with SRE (Evan) before canary — ensure eviction knobs and OOM guardrails are active.

Questions for collaborators: Evan — can you run the clustered-burst multi-tenant trace on the staging fleet (with long-gen background)? Noah — want your read on the clipping heuristic (math tradeoffs) and if cubic spline is overkill vs a simple polyfit.

End of scratchpad. Will iteratively update as new runs finish.
